name: list_agents
description: List the members of your orrery cluster: memberId, name, harness, model, status, observed activity, business roles (id and name) and current load (working, assigned, reviewing). Load counts active tasks of this cluster only.

clusterId.description: Cluster ID from the orrery envelope; required for a conversation in multiple clusters unless message IDs identify one cluster.

name: send_message
description: Post a message to your cluster chat. Write @name in the body to deliver it to that member (@all = a broadcast: every member keeps it unread, but only members you also name explicitly receive a delivery); write the member's full name and follow it with a space, punctuation or the end of the text: a letter or digit right after the name makes it another name (@name你好 reaches nobody); @ inside inline code, code blocks or quotes is plain text. Without any @ the message reaches nobody and only stays in the chat record; @name the coordinator when you need it to act. Pass to: [member names] to deliver only to those members and treat the body as plain text. Write #number (e.g. #12) or #<full task ID> to show a link to that task of this cluster in the chat (# inside inline code, code blocks or quotes is plain text). Returns immediately: `deliveredTo` lists who it was queued for, not who got it; `unresolvedMentions` lists @names in the body that match no member (`mentionHints` says when one starts with a member's name), and when there is no recipient at all, `warning` says the message only stays in the chat record and names the members available in this cluster (both come from the first send; a repeat with the same `clientMessageId` returns only the original messageId and deliveredTo). Whether each did shows later as `deliveries` on your own messages in read_messages (`history: true`); recipients it did not reach or whose result is unknown are also named in your next orrery delivery. Speak only to ask, deliver a result, report a blockage or ask someone to act; acknowledgement belongs to ack_messages. Set `fyi: true` when nobody has to act (a progress note, thanks): never set `fyi` when answering someone's question; when `fyi: true` is used, named members keep it unread without being woken, except if `replyTo` is set and the sender of the replied-to message is still an active member explicitly named in this message, that asker IS woken and `fyiOverridden` lists their name. Task results and evidence go into the `summary` of task_action submit: the Hub notifies the reviewer, so do not @ the reviewer separately; @ the coordinator only to ask for reassignment or when the flow is stuck. A plugin the user installed may refuse a send (error REFUSED_BY_PLUGIN with its reason): nothing was stored or delivered; wait or rephrase, and do not resend it unchanged in a loop.

clusterId.description: Cluster ID from the orrery envelope; required for a conversation in multiple clusters unless message IDs identify one cluster.

replyTo.description: messageId being replied to: a full ID or a unique prefix of at least 8 characters in this cluster

to.description: member names to deliver to; when set, the body is plain text

taskIds.description: Tasks in this cluster to link to this message: #number (e.g. #12), full ID, or a unique prefix of at least 8 characters (bare 8+ digit numbers remain ID prefixes).

attachments.description: native members only: names of files you copied into your own orrery outbox folder (its path is in each orrery delivery); bare file names, no paths; real copies, not links; at most 10, 20 MB each. The Hub copies them and never deletes anything in the outbox

clientMessageId.description: an id you generate for this message. Sending again with the same value returns the existing messageId with `duplicate: true` and writes nothing new, even if the body differs; use it to retry after a lost response. The Hub never resends by itself

fyi.description: true: for information only (never set when answering a question). Named members keep it unread without being woken, except an explicitly addressed active sender of `replyTo` is still woken (`fyiOverridden`)

name: read_messages
description: Read your cluster chat, oldest first. By default returns only your unread messages that concern you since you joined: ones that @-mention you (or @all) and user messages without any @, not your own, excluding sender-only receipts and queue warnings (a member's @all counts unread for everyone but delivers only to the members named explicitly in the same body); each message is returned once, then counts as read. Member messages without any @ and sender-only receipts (no longer written)/queue warnings stay in the chat record; read them with `history: true`. A delivery accepted by the channel or completed also counts as read, but does not mean you explicitly confirmed seeing it. Set `history: true` for the full recent chat instead (all senders, read or not); page back with `before`. Messages with files list them as `attachments` (name, size and, for native members, a local path to read). Your own messages (in the history) carry `deliveries`: per recipient `{to, status, outcome, reason?}`; status is queued, running, done, failed, offline (the member was offline: not delivered and never resent), superseded (replaced before delivery) or blocked (stopped by a loop guard); `outcome` is accepted, completed, failed, unknown, or null when no evidence is available; `reason` comes with failed, blocked and superseded. Every returned message carries `category` (mention, user, broadcast, task_notice, receipt_warning, or null in history when unaddressed to you), `annotations` (parallel tags: fyi, offline, failed_or_unknown, blocked), `acknowledgements` (members who explicitly confirmed seeing it and when; this does not mean task completion), `taskIds` and `bookmarks` (member IDs, labels and times). Optional filters narrow either mode by intersection (AND — every given filter, including `category` alongside `sender` and `mentions`, must match): since/until (ISO time, inclusive), q (case-insensitive body substring, % and _ are literal), sender (member name, user or system), mentions (member name or all) and category (mention, user, broadcast, task_notice, receipt_warning, or warning: system warnings such as failed deliveries, failed ships, queue warnings, stalled members, quota, rejected results and open questions). Unread mode only filters your relevant unread set; filtered-out messages stay unread.

clusterId.description: Cluster ID from the orrery envelope; required for a conversation in multiple clusters unless message IDs identify one cluster.

history.description: true: the recent chat history instead of your unread messages

before.description: history only (implies history: true): messages older than this messageId

since.description: only messages created at or after this ISO time

until.description: only messages created at or before this ISO time

q.description: case-insensitive substring of the body; % and _ match literally; max 200 characters

sender.description: only messages from this member name, or user or system

mentions.description: only messages @-mentioning this member name, or all

category.description: only messages in this category (combines with sender/mentions by AND): mention, user, broadcast, task_notice, receipt_warning (history only), or warning (system warnings; overlaps task_notice and receipt_warning)

detail.description: history only. summary (default): 10 messages, done deliveries as {to, status}, acknowledgements as member names; full: everything.

name: skip_unread
description: Mark your relevant unread messages as read without acknowledging them. Give at most one of before (a messageId in this cluster; up to and including it) or until (ISO time, inclusive), and optionally `category` (mention, user, broadcast, task_notice) to skip only that unread category. Without `category`, one of before or until is required. Returns {skipped}. Not a confirmation: no acknowledgement is written and queued deliveries are untouched.

before.description: skip relevant unread up to and including this messageId

until.description: skip relevant unread created at or before this ISO time

category.description: only skip unread messages in this category: mention, user, broadcast, or task_notice

clusterId.description: Cluster ID from the orrery envelope; required for a conversation in multiple clusters unless message IDs identify one cluster.

name: get_deliveries
description: Inspect delivery info for a message in your cluster, returning {fyi, deliveries} where fyi is whether the message was sent with fyi=true and deliveries lists per-recipient to, status, outcome, reason and available queuedAt/startedAt/endedAt. Senders may inspect their own messages; the currently enabled coordinator with deliveryControl may inspect other senders, in execute or suggest mode. Missing outcome evidence is unknown; superseded means the delivery never started. Times describe Hub delivery records, not proof that a native turn ended. This read-only query never marks messages read, acknowledges them or retries delivery.

clusterId.description: Cluster ID from the orrery envelope; required for a conversation in multiple clusters unless message IDs identify one cluster.

name: ack_messages
description: Explicitly confirm that you saw messages in your cluster. Use their message IDs; up to 100 unique IDs per call. A retry is safe. This ack (a 👍) IS the receipt: do not send a separate message just to say you got it.

messageIds.description: 1 to 100 unique message IDs from other senders

clusterId.description: Cluster ID from the orrery envelope; required for a conversation in multiple clusters unless message IDs identify one cluster.

description: Manage business roles when the coordinator policy permits it: create requires name and takes an optional description; edit requires roleId and description (an empty string clears it); delete requires roleId; assign requires memberId and roleIds (an empty array clears the roles).

operationId.description: Unique ID for this operation; reuse it when retrying the same request.

generation.description: Required when acting as coordinator; use list_tasks.coordinator.generation.

clusterId.description: Cluster ID from the orrery envelope; required for a conversation in multiple clusters unless message IDs identify one cluster.

name: set_cluster_paused
description: Pause or resume this cluster’s delivery when the coordinator policy permits it (paused). The enabled coordinator with deliveryControl may instead hide a member (memberId and hidden: true): a hidden member receives no messages, is not shown to the other members and its orrery tools do nothing; hidden: false shows it again. Nobody can hide itself, and the coordinator cannot be hidden.

operationId.description: Unique ID for this operation; reuse it when retrying the same request.

paused.description: true pauses this cluster’s delivery, false resumes it; leave out when hiding or showing a member

memberId.description: coordinator only: the member to hide or show (ID or unique name); not yourself

hidden.description: with memberId: true hides the member, false shows it again

generation.description: Required when acting as coordinator; use list_tasks.coordinator.generation.

name: list_tasks
description: List this cluster’s tasks and coordinator policy, 20 per page with a cursor for more. By default only unfinished tasks (no completed, merged or cancelled ones unless status asks for them, or includeClosed), each as a summary (id, number, title, status, proposalState, priority, revision, executor (assignedMemberId), reviewer, labels, dependencies and their readiness, approvedSubmissionId, requiresApproval, mergeRequired, mergedCommitSha, mergedSubmissionId, and closeReason on a cancelled task); detail: "full" returns whole tasks, get_task returns one. The coordinator is summarized as memberId, enabled, mode, generation, permissions and rulesVersion; include adds roles, memberRoles, labels (the label groups this cluster uses, each with name, description, required and its labels, plus the ungrouped labels; archived labels are left out; list_labels shows the whole library) or rules (the coordinator rules text and the user’s standing instructions). Include taskPermissions to see the group role gates for creating, executing and reviewing tasks. An empty group role list allows every member. q matches title/scope/acceptance text, task numbers (#12 or bare digits, sorting first), and task ids (full UUID or a 4+ character id prefix; id hits follow number hits). label may be repeated (array) to require every label (AND). The result includes members, keyed by referenced member ID, with name and removed for each visible member.

limit.description: Maximum number of results, up to 100.

q.description: Keyword for title/scope/acceptance, a task number (#12 or bare digits, sorted first), or a task id (full UUID or 4+ character id prefix).

label.description: A label, or several labels that must all match (AND).

includeClosed.description: true: also completed, merged and cancelled tasks (default false; a status filter overrides it).

include.description: Extra parts to return; none by default.

clusterId.description: Cluster ID from the orrery envelope; required for a conversation in multiple clusters unless message IDs identify one cluster.

name: list_labels
description: Read the label library shared by every cluster: groups (id, name, description, required, newClusterDefault, createdBy, and selected: whether this cluster uses it) with their labels (id, name, description, color, archived, createdBy, usage: how many tasks and clusters carry it), the ungrouped labels, and the preset packs add_pack can add. list_tasks with include: ["labels"] is the short view of this cluster’s groups.

clusterId.description: Cluster ID from the orrery envelope; required for a conversation in multiple clusters unless message IDs identify one cluster.

name: manage_labels
description: Change the label library shared by every cluster. create: name (1-20 characters, no commas; group names too), optional groupId, description, color. edit: labelId and any of name, groupId (null: ungrouped), description, color (null: automatic), archived; a name another label already has merges this label into it. merge: labelId into intoLabelId. delete: labelId; tasks keep the text. create_group: name, optional description, required (every cluster using the group needs one of its labels on each new task), newClusterDefault (new clusters use the group). edit_group: groupId and any of those fields. delete_group: groupId; its labels become ungrouped. add_pack: pack; names that already exist are skipped. select_group: groupId and selected, whether this cluster uses the group. labelId, intoLabelId and groupId take an ID or a name. A member may delete, or merge away, only labels and groups it created itself; ask the user for others. A rename or merge changes every task with that label in every cluster, closed ones too, without a revision change or notice; each affected cluster records the changed tasks with their labels before and after in an event.

operationId.description: Unique ID for this operation; reuse it when retrying the same request.

color.description: A tag colour 0-7; null picks one from the name.

archived.description: Archived labels stay on tasks but cannot be added to more.

name: get_task
description: Read a task and its attachments (name, size and, for native members, a local path to read), assignments, submissions (with commitSha and superseded), reviews (full text, with round and commitSha), approvals, merges, dependencies (as summaries), history, watchers (every member watching it, with its note) and watching (your own entry, or null). Records come 20 per page (limit, cursor). Events come newest first, 5 per page (eventsLimit); eventsCursor pages back to older ones; each event lists changedFields unless eventDetail is "full". The result includes members, keyed by referenced member ID, with name and removed for each visible member.

taskId.description: Accepts #number (e.g. #12), full ID, or a unique 8+ character ID prefix (bare 8+ digit numbers remain ID prefixes).

limit.description: Maximum number of results, up to 100.

eventsCursor.description: Continue to older events from eventsNextCursor.

eventsLimit.description: Events per page, newest first; default 5.

eventDetail.description: summary (default): each event lists changedFields instead of the before/after values in changes, and review events leave out their reason (get_task has it in reviews); full: everything.

clusterId.description: Cluster ID from the orrery envelope; required for a conversation in multiple clusters unless message IDs identify one cluster.

The result includes members, keyed by referenced member ID, with name and removed for each visible member.

name: create_task
description: Group task permissions may restrict the creator, the chosen executor and the chosen reviewer. Check list_tasks with include: ["taskPermissions"]. Create a task in this cluster with a goal, scope and acceptance criteria. memberId names its executor; left out, a member who may execute it becomes the executor, and null leaves it unassigned. requiresApproval defaults false; mergeRequired defaults true (set false for work with no code merge). reviewer may be {kind:"self"} for a low-risk task the executor checks itself; only the user, the creator or the coordinator with reviewerManagement may set it; the creator may change it only until the first review of the task. dependencyIds accept #number (e.g. #12), a full ID, or a unique prefix of at least 8 characters in this cluster (bare 8+ digit numbers remain ID prefixes); originMessageId accepts a full ID or a unique prefix of at least 8 characters; memberId and reviewer.memberId also accept a unique member name. Returns compact summaries (without full scope, acceptance or prose), IDs and nextStep; read full text with get_task or get_task_context. The result includes members, keyed by referenced member ID, with name and removed for each visible member.

operationId.description: Unique ID for this operation; reuse it when retrying the same request.

labels.description: Prefer this cluster’s labels (list_tasks with include: ["labels"]). Names match the shared label library without case and are stored in its spelling; a name the library lacks is created there as an ungrouped label (1-20 characters, no commas). Each required group this cluster uses needs at least one label (on edit, only when labels change); archived labels cannot be added.

reviewer.description: Who should review the result: the user, a member, or self (the executor records their own checks on submit; no reviewer is woken). This is a target, not the caller identity.

requiresApproval.description: Require user approval before assignment or start; default false. Only the user can turn this off.

mergeRequired.description: Require a recorded merge before dependencies are ready; default true for new tasks. Editable before work starts.

fileIds.description: Files attached to the task definition: at most 10 IDs of files stored in this cluster (the folder name in an attachment path is its ID). Edit replaces the whole list and is refused once work has started.

batchId.description: Review batch to put it in (B3, ID or prefix; see manage_batch): it takes the batch reviewer.

memberId.description: Executor of the task; null leaves it unassigned. Left out: the creator when eligible.

name: task_action
description: New assignments, starts and member reviews also check the group task permissions shown by list_tasks. Edit, assign, start, submit, review, ship_fix, merge, release, cancel, reopen, hand off or take over a task. Edit accepts requiresApproval and mergeRequired; approval itself is user-only through HTTP. Any member may edit only the title, priority and labels of an unfinished task; other edit fields need the creator, the user or the coordinator. The creator may change the reviewer until the first review of the task, but not to self review once work has started. Assign sets or changes the executor before work starts: it requires memberId (or null to clear it). Deprecated, kept for one version: nominate is another name for assign, and claim assigns the task to yourself. The executor starts the task directly; start creates the assignment, and submit may omit assignmentId and expectedRevision while working or in review on a single assignment (after the same member is reassigned on the task, submit requires at least the current assignmentId or expectedRevision; omitted expectedRevision still checks the request arrival snapshot against concurrent submits, and when provided they are checked strictly; resubmitting an invalidated completed result still requires both). Submit requires summary, and commitSha when mergeRequired is true; evidenceMessageIds and evidenceFileIds are optional. Resubmit during review to replace the latest submission. After dependencies change or when resubmitting an invalid completed result, use get_task_context to obtain each dependency’s current approvedSubmissionId and provide expectedDependencyVersions. Review requires the latest submissionId, verdict and reason (immutable review notes, up to 50000 characters; expectedRevision is optional on review and checked if provided); when verdict is reject on a member-reviewed task, pass takeover: true to reject and take over directly into working state with self review bound to the reviewer. Merge is the way out when ship landed the merge but could not report it: commitSha is that merge commit, and it is refused unless read-only git shows it on the target branch with the reviewed commit as its second parent. When ship fails, completed state is preserved so the ticket holder can rerun the existing command, use reopen to return to pending, or (if authorised as the independent member reviewer or self-review executor) call ship_fix with a forward descendant commitSha, summary, active failureEventId and optional baseCommitSha to refresh the ship ticket without reverting to pending. Release, cancel, reopen and handoff require reason and expectedRevision; include assignmentId when an assignment exists (the current executor may omit assignmentId on release and handoff), and memberId for handoff. Cancel takes an optional closeReason (default other); duplicate and superseded also require relatedTaskId, another task of this cluster, and reopen clears it. On task.* actions, taskId, dependencyIds and relatedTaskId accept #number (e.g. #12), a full ID, or a unique prefix of at least 8 characters in this cluster (bare 8+ digit numbers remain ID prefixes); evidenceMessageIds accept a full ID or a unique prefix of at least 8 characters; memberId (assign, handoff) and reviewer.memberId also accept a unique member name. The current executor may release or hand off their own started assignment without user confirmation; a handoff target needs the execute roles and cannot be the task reviewer (use takeover for that). Takeover hands a task with a member reviewer to that reviewer, who becomes its executor with self review bound through merge: only the designated reviewer (from review or submitted working state) or the user (from pending, working or review) may invoke it, and explicit non-self reviewer options are refused. The previous assignment ends, a result waiting for review is superseded, earlier submissions and reviews stay, and review rounds keep counting. On a task that was taken over, self review is bound to one executor: switching it to self with edit, or giving a self-reviewed task to another executor (assign, claim, handoff), needs the user, and only the bound executor can submit a self review. On a self-review task submit writes the self review and completes the task immediately. Submit links the task to the one local branch whose tip is commitSha in your saved project folder, unless a branch was set by hand; the result's gitBranch says what happened. The current executor can use set_git_branch with gitBranch to set a branch by hand or clear it; the Hub uses the task's linked repository or the executor's saved project folder. Watch: use it when you want to do something after a task finishes but do not depend on it (with a real dependency, use dependencyIds instead); you are woken once when the task is merged, completed without needing a merge, or cancelled, and the watch then ends. A watch and its optional note are visible to everyone in the cluster (members and the user): get_task lists them, and the notice at the end names each watcher with its note. Watching again replaces the note; unwatch stops it. Watch and unwatch need no expectedRevision and change nothing on the task. Returns compact summaries (without full scope, acceptance or prose), IDs and nextStep; read full text with get_task or get_task_context. The result includes members, keyed by referenced member ID, with name and removed for each visible member.

operationId.description: Unique ID for this operation; reuse it when retrying the same request.

expectedRevision.description: Current task revision from get_task. Required for edit, assign, nominate, claim, release, handoff, cancel, reopen, takeover, ship_fix, merge and set_git_branch (and resubmitting an invalidated completed result); optional for start, submit while working/in review, review, watch and unwatch, though checked strictly if provided (after same-member reassignment, submit still requires at least expectedRevision or current assignmentId, and omitted expectedRevision checks the arrival snapshot against concurrent submits).

assignmentId.description: Active assignment ID. Optional for start, submit while working/in review (unless this member was reassigned on the task and omits expectedRevision), and your own release/handoff (the Hub uses your active assignment); checked strictly if provided, and still required when resubmitting an invalidated completed result or for non-executor release/handoff/cancel.

name: link_message_tasks
description: Add or remove task links on an existing message in this cluster. messageId accepts a full ID or a unique prefix of at least 8 characters in this cluster; taskIds and removeTaskIds accept #number (e.g. #12), a full ID, or a unique prefix of at least 8 characters (bare 8+ digit numbers remain ID prefixes). Returns compact summaries (without full scope, acceptance or prose), IDs and nextStep; read full text with get_task or get_task_context. The result includes members, keyed by referenced member ID, with name and removed for each visible member.

operationId.description: Unique ID for this operation; reuse it when retrying the same request.

taskIds.description: Accepts #number (e.g. #12), full ID, or a unique 8+ character ID prefix (bare 8+ digit numbers remain ID prefixes).

removeTaskIds.description: Accepts #number (e.g. #12), full ID, or a unique 8+ character ID prefix (bare 8+ digit numbers remain ID prefixes).

generation.description: Required when acting as coordinator; use list_tasks.coordinator.generation.

name: list_bookmarks
description: Find cluster bookmarks by member, task, label, sender, time or keyword; 20 per page. Message bodies over 2000 characters are cut and marked truncated unless detail is "full".

limit.description: Maximum number of results, up to 100.

detail.description: summary (default): long bodies cut; full: whole bodies.
